cards.text: David is the new king over all Israel (1 Chronicles 11:3). Now we meet his mighty men, the chiefs who, together with all Israel, strengthened his kingdom, according to the word of the LORD. Friend, I once lost a tug-of-war to a rubber band in that junk drawer, so these guys already scare me.
First on the list is Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, chief of the officers. One man. One spear. And a WHOLE lot of opponents.

cards.question: Jashobeam wields his spear against ___ hundred men and kills them at one time.

cards.text: Next in command is Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men, and he's with David at Pas-dammim when the Philistines gather for battle at a field full of barley. Friend, the biggest battle I ever fought was a stuck junk drawer, and the drawer WON.

cards.question: When the Philistines come at the barley field at Pas-dammim, the troops hold their ground.
The troops flee the barley field at Pas-dammim. What do Eleazar and David do?

answers.text: Stand in the middle of the field and defend it
Chase after the troops to bring them back
Set fire to the barley and slip away

cards.question: Eleazar and David strike down the Philistines, and the ___ brings about a great victory.

cards.text: Another time, three of the thirty chief men go down to David at the rock at the cave of Adullam, while a company of Philistines is camped in the Valley of Rephaim. David's in the stronghold, the Philistines have a garrison at Bethlehem, and I bet nobody in that cave is sleeping much, and I'm nervous just TELLING it.
David longs for water, and he says it out loud. He wishes someone would get him a drink from one particular well.

cards.question: David wishes someone would bring him a drink of water. Where is the well he's thinking of?

cards.text: So the Three break right through the Philistine camp, draw water from that well, and carry it back to David. Friend, I've been wishing out loud for somebody to scrub my cookie sheets for YEARS, and nobody moves... because I live alone.

cards.question: The Three hand David water they got by breaking through a Philistine camp. What does David do with it?

answers.text: He pours it out to the LORD
He gives it to the troops

cards.question: David refuses to drink the water from Bethlehem because the men risked their lives to bring it.

cards.text: Then David says, "Far be it from me, my God, to do this! How can I drink the blood of these men who risked their lives?" Such were the exploits of the three mighty men.
Now meet Abishai, the brother of Joab, and he's chief of the Three. He wields his spear against three hundred men, kills them, and wins a name along with the Three, so that's three hundred AGAIN.

cards.question: Abishai, the chief of the Three, is officially included among the Three.

cards.text: Abishai is doubly honored and leads the Three without ever being one of them. Next up is Benaiah son of Jehoiada from Kabzeel, a man of valor and a man of many exploits.

cards.question: Benaiah strikes down two champions. Which nation are they from?
On a snowy day, Benaiah goes down into a pit and kills a ___.

cards.text: Then there's an Egyptian, a huge man five cubits tall, holding a spear like a weaver's beam, and Benaiah goes against him with a club. A CLUB, friend, and I'd have taken one look at that spear and dived face-first into the chocolate chips.

cards.question: Benaiah has a club. The huge Egyptian has a spear like a weaver's beam. How does Benaiah win?

answers.text: He snatches the spear and kills him with it
He knocks the spear away and the Egyptian runs
He calls the Three to fight beside him

cards.question: Benaiah is the most honored among the Thirty, and he becomes one of the Three.
After all his exploits, David appoints Benaiah over his ___.

cards.text: Then comes the long roll call of the mighty men, from Asahel the brother of Joab down to Jaasiel the Mezobaite, with names like Zelek the Ammonite, Ithmah the Moabite and Uriah the Hittite. I can't pronounce half these names, friend, and every one of them could beat me at arm wrestling, and my arms are a MUSTACHE.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: "First on the list is Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, chief of the officers." "One man." "One spear." "And a WHOLE lot of opponents." Only the opening card may run longer than two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card packs in more than two beats: three chief men come to David at Adullam, Philistines are camped in the Valley of Rephaim, David is in the stronghold, there is a garrison at Bethlehem, plus a guessed feeling and a joke. It should be split.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: "Another time" says this happened on a separate occasion. The text (1 Chronicles 11:15) gives no timing. It only says three of the thirty chief men went down to David.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The closing line "and I'm nervous just TELLING it" is pleasant, but it doesn't land as a real laugh.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The tag "so that's three hundred AGAIN" only observes the repeat. It isn't a laugh-out-loud moment.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The joke adds a new event to the junk drawer backstory: losing a tug-of-war to a rubber band. The backstory mentions rubber band stretching contests, not Papa Dorin losing a tug-of-war. Made-up joke moments are allowed only around his bakery.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The joke adds a new event to the junk drawer backstory: Papa Dorin fought a stuck junk drawer and lost. This is not in his backstory, and it is not a bakery moment.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: Joab appears here for the first time ("Abishai, the brother of Joab") but is never introduced. 1 Chronicles 11:6 makes him David's chief commander.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The story card before this question calls Abishai "chief of the Three," which points the baker toward True. The right answer is False (1 Chronicles 11:21). Nothing earlier lets a baker reason out that he isn't one of the Three, so the setup steers them to the wrong pick.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: Most of the stop's choice cards are pure discovery that no earlier card sets up: Abishai not being among the Three (card 2), the champions being from Moab (card 4), the lion (card 5), snatching the Egyptian's spear (card 7) and the guard (card 9). Most choice cards here are luck, not informed guesses.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "army" is arguable. 1 Chronicles 27:5 names Benaiah son of Jehoiada as an army commander under David, so a baker could argue David put him over the army.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
